# doit_composer_recipe_results (Data Source)

Beta. Read-only access to Composer recipes and their results. A recipe evaluates your cloud resources against a set of conditions; each result is a finding on one affected resource, and published recipes surface as proprietary Insights in the Console.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Retrieve all results for a Composer recipe
data "doit_composer_recipe_results" "all" {
  recipe_id = 569
}

# Filter for active results only, sorted by detection time
data "doit_composer_recipe_results" "active" {
  recipe_id  = 569
  filter     = "status:active"
  sort_by    = "detection_time"
  sort_order = "desc"
}

output "result_count" {
  value = data.doit_composer_recipe_results.all.row_count
}

output "active_findings" {
  value = [for res in data.doit_composer_recipe_results.active.items : {
    id                   = res.id
    account_id           = res.account_id
    issued_resource_name = res.issued_resource_name
    provider             = res.provider
    region               = res.region
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `recipe_id` (Number) ID of the Composer recipe whose results to list. Get recipe IDs from `GET /insights/v2/recipes`.

### Optional

- `filter` (String) Restricts the results returned. One string of `key:value` clauses: `,` separates alternative values for one key (OR) and `|` separates keys (AND). For example, `region:us-east-1,us-west-2|status:active` returns active results in either region. Because `,` and `|` are separators, a value itself can't contain them. Matching is exact unless a key says otherwise. Omit `filter` to list the recipe's results from the most recent scan of each recently scanned account, in every status.

Keys:
- `account_id`: one or more cloud account IDs, matched exactly.
- `region`: one or more cloud regions, matched exactly.
- `issued_resource_name`: one or more names of the affected resource, matched exactly.
- `related_resource_name`: one or more names of resources related to the result (for example, an attached IAM policy). Each value is matched as a substring anywhere in the result's related-resource details, not only against names.
- `status`: exactly one of `active` (not resolved and not snoozed), `snoozed`, `resolved` or `all`. Omitting it is the same as `all`. Combine `resolved` with `last_scan_only:false`; with the default it usually returns nothing.
- `last_scan_only`: exactly one of `true` or `false`. Defaults to `true`, which returns only results reported by each recently scanned account's most recent scan. A resolved result keeps the ID of the last scan that reported it, so resolved results rarely appear by default. `false` returns results from every scan and account, including resolved ones.
- `allocation`: up to 10 distinct allocation IDs (duplicates are ignored); get allocation IDs from `GET /analytics/v1/allocations`. Matches results on resources in any of those allocations, as resolved by Cloud Analytics; `rowCount` then counts only those results. You must be able to view every listed allocation. Service-account API keys can use public allocations only. If allocation access can't be checked, the request returns `503` with `Retry-After` and never falls back to unfiltered data.

Errors:
- An unknown key returns `400 filter_key_not_supported` when it's the only problem, otherwise `400 validation_failed`.
- A `status` outside the allowed list, a non-boolean `last_scan_only`, more than one `status` or `last_scan_only` value, more than 10 distinct allocation IDs, an invalid allocation ID (blank, longer than 256 characters, or containing `/`, whitespace or control characters), a malformed expression or an unsupported operator returns `400 validation_failed`.
- An allocation that doesn't exist or that you can't view returns `404 composer-api.allocation_not_found`.
- `max_results` (Number) Maximum number of items to return on one page, from 1 to 500. Defaults to 50. A value outside that range returns `400 validation_failed`.
- `page_token` (String) Continuation token from the `pageToken` of the previous response. Omit it on the first request; a response without `pageToken` is the last page.

The token records the position, the sort and the `allocation` filter IDs. Changing `sortBy`, `sortOrder` or the allocation IDs while paginating returns `400 pagination_token_invalid`. Keep the other `filter` keys and `maxResults` unchanged while paginating. Tokens expire 5 minutes after they are issued; an expired token returns `400 pagination_token_expired`. In both cases, restart from the first page.
- `sort_by` (String) Field to sort results by. Defaults to `detection_time`. Ties break by `id` (ascending), whatever the `sortOrder`.
Possible values: `detection_time`, `resolved_time`, `account_id`, `region`, `resource_class`, `cost_estimation_potential_savings`, `cost_estimation_potential_increased_costs`, `cost_estimation_potential_freed_commitments`, `cost_estimation_potential_increased_commitments_required`
- `sort_order` (String) Sort direction for `sortBy`. Defaults to `desc`.
Possible values: `asc`, `desc`
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) Results on this page. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))
- `row_count` (Number) Total number of results across all pages.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `account_id` (String) Cloud account the affected resource belongs to (for example, an AWS account ID or a Google Cloud project ID).
- `cost_estimation_potential_freed_commitments` (Number) Freed commitments — the daily amount in US dollars of commitment coverage (Savings Plans, Reserved Instances or CUDs) that acting on this result frees up for other usage. The Console **Freed commitments** column is this daily US-dollar amount × 365, converted to your organization's currency. Absent when not estimated, and always absent on resolved results.
- `cost_estimation_potential_increased_commitments_required` (Number) Avoidable commitments — the daily amount in US dollars of extra commitment or overlapping cost you avoid by timing the action, for example to a Reserved Instance's expiry. The Console **Avoidable commitments** column is this daily US-dollar amount × 365, converted to your organization's currency. Absent when not estimated, and always absent on resolved results.
- `cost_estimation_potential_increased_costs` (Number) Cost avoidance — the daily amount in US dollars of a future charge (for example, extended-support fees) you prevent by acting on this result in time. The Console **Cost avoidance** column is this daily US-dollar amount × 365, converted to your organization's currency. Absent when not estimated, and always absent on resolved results.
- `cost_estimation_potential_savings` (Number) Potential cost savings — the daily amount in US dollars you would stop paying by acting on this result. The Console **Cost savings** column is this daily US-dollar amount × 365, converted to your organization's currency. Absent when not estimated, and always absent on resolved results.
- `detection_time` (String) When the result was first detected (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `first_flow_id` (String) ID of the Composer scan that first reported this result. Absent when unknown.
- `id` (Number) Result ID.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the result's account was scanned recently. It does not say whether the result is resolved or snoozed; use `solved` and `snoozed` for that, or the `status` filter.
- `issued_resource_id` (String) Identifier of the affected resource, as stored by Composer.
- `issued_resource_name` (String) Name of the affected resource.
- `last_flow_id` (String) ID of the most recent Composer scan that reported this result. Absent when unknown.
- `provider` (String) Cloud provider or platform, using the Console's provider names.
- `provider_identifier` (String) Canonical cloud-provider identifier of the affected resource.
- AWS: the resource's ARN when one is available, otherwise the stored identifier (for example, an EC2 instance ID).
- Google Cloud: the API relative resource name (for example, `projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances/vm-1`), or the bucket name for Cloud Storage; otherwise the stored identifier.
- Other providers: the provider-native identifier.

`null` when no identifier is stored or it could not be resolved; resolving it never fails the request.
- `region` (String) Cloud region of the affected resource. Absent for global resources.
- `resolved_time` (String) When the result was resolved (RFC 3339, UTC). Absent while unresolved.
- `resource_class` (String) Type of the affected resource. Absent when unknown.
- `rule_id` (Number) ID of the recipe the result belongs to. Equal to the `recipeId` path parameter.
- `snoozed` (Boolean) Whether the result is currently snoozed. Present only when `true`; absent means not snoozed.
- `solved` (Boolean) Whether the result is resolved.
- `tags` (Map of String) Cloud-provider tags on the affected resource, as key/value pairs. An empty object means the resource has no tags. `null` means the tags could not be resolved; resolving them never fails the request.
